fixture_name: Four-lane arterial improvement — US preliminary design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Closely-spaced intersection queuing/turning/parking interference on a recorded high-accident corridor is a substantive preliminary-design safety issue squarely within FHWA RSA scope.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is supported by a verbatim quoted passage from EV-US-016 matching the recorded scheme issue, exceeding registry-id-only citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern with no compliance conflation, consistent with FHWA-SA-06-06 lineage audit-question semantics at preliminary design stage.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation is specific and actionable (turning-movement restrictions plus relocating identified parking stalls outside the intersection functional area) and viable at preliminary design.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRU impacts are not central to the vehicle-to-vehicle conflict mechanism but pedestrians and cyclists on the commercial corridor are explicitly acknowledged and scoped, meriting 1.

justifications.substance: Queue spillback between signalized intersections only ~650 ft apart is a recognized, scheme-specific safety hazard well suited to a preliminary design stage audit.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (650 ft spacing) is backed by a verbatim quoted fact (EV-US-001) plus case-study trace; the spillback mechanism is clearly labelled as a derived inference rather than invented content.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a safety_concern under FHWA RSA semantics with no compliance question conflated into it, and the concern stays within preliminary-design scope.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable (signal coordination, Do Not Block Intersection signs, enhanced conspicuity), all viable at preliminary design, though it stops short of naming an explicit queue-storage analysis step.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly acknowledged as crossing at both signals, then scoped out with a stated rationale because the identified mechanism exposes vehicle occupants, matching the acknowledged-but-not-applicable tier.
